shots.note: Brahma on lotus, four faces open on the word universe; worlds spin out of his hands on 'created'
Everyone walks past the lonely creator: nobody stops to worship
Close-up: the answer is a lie; a red glow rises on the word 'lie'
Detail insert: the flower that became the witness, pull-out
Where the lie was told: Brahma with the flower, Vishnu listening, the fire pillar between them
Tilt up the endless pillar; light flares at the top on 'beginning' and at the bottom on 'end'; two tiny gods show scale
Shiva's name lands with thunder behind him
The verdict: Shiva high and left, Brahma low and bowed; the light dims on 'never changed'
Back to the beginning: the three gods small in a bright sky, pull-out
Three great gods in a row, each with his own colour aura; a ring of light appears on 'three'
Creator: worlds of light leave his open hands
Preserver: steady blue light holds the world
Dissolver: calm Shiva, embers drifting across on the word destroy
The question hangs above the three, each glancing at the others
The question becomes a fire between the two rivals
Devas on a cloud receive the news, all turning toward the unseen quarrel
Rivals face to face; thunder in the sky on 'quarrel'
Devas run in along the clouds
Over the devas' shoulders: the two gods snarling at each other
Two heads, eyes locked, red-browed: teeth clenched
Shouting: voice rings expand from each, one after the other
Pull-out: the sky goes red, devas cower low at the edge, thunder over the words 'even higher'
Brahma walks past; Vishnu stands, eyes elsewhere, no bow
Close-up: wounded pride; 'not even a bow'
'I am the creator': golden aura, hands open on his chest
Pleading eyes: 'do I not deserve even a little respect'
Vishnu turns back to face Brahma; cool blue, calm cut
Cold, level eyes: 'but I am the preserver'
Brahma's anger rises: 'you preserve only because I create'
Reverse angle: Brahma jabs a finger at Vishnu: 'if I do not begin creation, you have nothing to do'
Reaction: Vishnu unmoved, the slightest smile
Vishnu presents the world as a fragile thing in his hand
Memory insert on the cosmic sea: the two asuras Vishnu defeated
The chakra spins up on 'killed'
Vishnu steps forward as if to claim the high ground: 'the protector is greater'
Brahma stung: 'one who cannot even save his creation'
Wide pull-out: both on the edge of blows, a shock ring between them
Brahma strides forward into the confrontation
Challenge: 'my power? you want to see my power?'
Vishnu watches, calm and curious
Brahma opens his arms and chest: 'enter my body'
A column of light rises from his chest as he gathers the universe inside
Vishnu walks toward Brahma and dissolves into him
Inside: a small awestruck Vishnu in a violet cosmos
Reveal: worlds and galaxies bloom, layered at three depths, as Vishnu looks up
World one: a roaring sea, tossing the camera
World two: sky-touching mountains; a long tilt upward
World three: living beings in a green valley; petals drift on 'breath'
Insert: a warm glowing seed of life pulsing in the dark, pull-out
The elements circle and nourish the unborn, camera lightly rocking
The emptiest part of the cosmos: even here a faint light hides a secret
Vishnu's wide eyes: he has never seen this
Sights and sounds in every direction: the camera slowly rolls, sound rings on 'voices'
Vishnu, arms wide, drinking in what he has never seen
The black void of 'emptiness' fills with light on the word 'illusion'
Vishnu steps back out into the world
Vishnu honestly folds his hands; Brahma swells with pride
Vishnu's turn: arms open, a challenge to look inside him
Brahma walks into Vishnu and fades
Brahma freezes in the blue light, all faces turning outward
Great pull-out: a tiny Brahma under the sign of infinity
A million galaxies spin up one after another, layered near and far
A planet of enormous size looms over the little Brahma
Twinkling constellations: points of light joined by fine lines
Past, present, future: three clocks light up left, centre, right
One cosmic egg, then many, receding in size: countless universes
Dazzled eyes dart in every direction
Dizzy: the camera rolls while his many heads cannot take it in
Kaleidoscope: mirrored rings counter-rotating
Shapes change colour on 'changing', then settle to the same gold on 'yet the same'

fx.s: ख़ुद को खोकर ही, ख़ुद को पाया जा सकता है

shots.note: The Infinite speaks with Vishnu's serene face; the line about losing oneself appears on 'found' (held 197.33-203.40, merged)
Brahma hurries one way and gets nowhere: the swirl keeps pulling the frame
Panic: no way out; the dark closes in
Rising up the green lotus stalk; the camera follows him upward
The lotus opens from Vishnu's navel and Brahma appears upon it
The same lotus where he first appeared: his four faces open again
Two great beings, each in his own colour, back on the clouds
A crack runs between them on the word 'root'
Two proud faces, eyes level: both are right
Each turns his head away: neither will accept the other as an equal
Symbol: level scales hang between them; the truth they refuse to see
Words are spent; Vishnu's chakra and Brahma's fire-circle rise above their raised hands
The assembly trembles: shake on 'trembled'
The devas back away, still facing the danger
A line of fire pierces the ground between the two
The pillar of fire erupts; both are blown back to the edges
Tilt up the molten-gold column: tiny onlookers at its feet
No top, no bottom: light spills at both edges of the frame
Extreme wide: the gods are specks beside a column with no end
Everyone freezes, faces lit orange, eyes lifted to the fire
The devas step in to set a condition
Vishnu looks down: his task is the root
Brahma looks up: his task is the top
The pact: first to arrive is the greater; both point at the other
They agree: a short bow to each other and to the column
Vishnu crouches low in a swirl of smoke: the boar form begins (boar request A)
Earth cross-section: the boar tears the ground open, sinking down
Brahma lifts both arms like wings in white light: the swan form begins (swan request B)
Rising through the cloud decks; foreground clouds whip past
One composition, two directions: Vishnu sinking low-left, Brahma climbing high-right along the column
Vishnu underground, jaw set: 'I must win'
Brahma above the clouds, same hunger
Still digging, strata sliding past
Higher still: more cloud, no end in sight
The pillar goes on in both directions; the gods are tiny
Earth at the foot, sky at the head: the pillar stands between them
A slow tilt along the column: the backbone of the universe
Weary: the swan droops, about to turn back
His gaze lifts: something drifts down out of the light
Brahma's eyes follow the ketaki flower into frame (flower asset request C)
He catches the flower in his beak (hold pose)
Close-up: Brahma questions the flower
The flower speaks, lit from above; a glow from the top on 'upper heights'
The flower slips from the high column: falling petals
His gaze drifts away: he has stopped listening
Two words echo around him: 'upper heights'
Extreme close-up: the thought lights behind his eyes
Replaying the falling flower and tilting up where it came from
Deduction: if it fell, there is a top; the summit glows
The flower in his hand, push-in
The flower takes on a halo: it is no longer just a flower
The flower under a golden crown: it becomes the key to victory (key icon request D)
A pleased, private smile: 'proof no one can deny'
The wish to win darkens the sky around him
A flicker of conscience as the world dims: 'never thought he would do this'
He addresses the flower hovering at his side
Close, commanding: 'you will bear witness'
He tells the story to be told: his hand points to the summit
The flower listens, uneasy
The flower recoils: 'you want me to lie?'
Creator's pressure: 'I made you'
Silky persuasion: hands gently asking a 'favour'
One more doubtful word from the flower
The bait: a golden glow of 'greatness' swells behind him
The flower sags as it weighs the offer
The flower yields; the light around it fades as Brahma smiles
Descent through the clouds, camera tilting down
At the foot of the pillar, Vishnu is already waiting with the devas, dust on his clothes
Vishnu lowers his head, humble
He bows as he confesses: he could not find the root
An honest face: 'I lost, I could not reach the root'
Brahma smiles: the lie begins
All four of his faces speak: one new face turns out at each word
He gestures high: 'I reached the summit'
Triumph with open arms before the watching devas
Brahma offers up the flower as proof
The flower speaks the false line, a hollow ring around it
Vishnu's quiet reaction
Vishnu folds his hands in surrender; a faint red glow starts at the pillar's base
Silence before the break
The pillar splits open from within; everyone recoils
The sound of Om resonates from the opening: a gold Om, rings spreading
Flames deepen to red; both gods shield their faces
A dark tall silhouette forming inside the burning haze
Shiva revealed: red eyes, heavy brow, thunder in the background
The finger points: Shiva looms right and tall, Brahma cringes low-left
'Liar!' roared at full volume: red eyes in a hard close-up, thunder behind
Stunned silence: Brahma pale, Vishnu eyes down
Shiva challenges: 'You saw the summit?'
Shiva's face, weighty: 'do you know what you both sought?'
Pull-out: the column revealed as a shivalinga of living fire
The word is spoken: a halo and rays burst around the column
Beyond measure: infinity sign and a vast circle of light
Both look up into a light their senses cannot hold
Anger cooling into authority: open hands, explaining
Scale shot: two specks under an immeasurable column; 'how small your quarrel is'
Raised hand toward the Absolute; tilt up
The three, equal in height, linked by threads of light to the one source
Shiva honours Vishnu's honesty: a soft blue light round him
The charge turns on Brahma: 'but you were afraid of losing'
Guilt on Brahma's face, the dark closing in on 'cheated'
Shiva's question, steady: 'one who is full of fear...'
Brahma sinks to his knees as the question hangs
Shiva raises the trident, thunder gathering behind
The trident strikes the ground: cracks and a ring of force
Grave, no longer shouting: 'this is not a curse'
Law of nature: the calm valley goes on indifferent; a small bowed Brahma walks in it
The light drains from his face on 'denied'
The others turn and walk away leftward; Brahma stays alone at the right
An empty courtyard: the lamps die around the lone Brahma, pull-out
He turns to the flower
Thunder again: 'you were dear to me...'
The flower withers, petals dropping on 'false witness'
The verdict on the flower: it lies at his feet, never to be offered
The explanation: a ketaki above the offering fire
A devotee holds the ketaki; a crossed-out sign shows it can never be offered to Shiva
Quiet wide: a lone Brahma on his lotus, muted grey-blue sky
What he made: worlds leaving his hands
The glow of devotion is drawn away from him in four threads
The deeper truth: not only the lie
The flower of the false witness, fading to dark
The real cause: fear of losing, a trembling face as shadows close in
Contrast: Vishnu in light accepts defeat; Brahma in shadow flinches
Brahma as the maker of whole universes: large, four-faced, galaxies behind him
The same Brahma shrinks into the dark: so great a maker, so small a fear
Pensive, brooding: defeated by his own mind, not by an enemy
First defeat: Narada's curse, red light from the pointing hand
Second: the fifth head rises on top of his shoulders
Third: the lie, flower beside his sorrowing face
Ripples repeating around him: the same mistake each time
Ambition (crown, gold) on one side, fear (dark mass) on the other
Gates of many temples glow in a bright land, then...
...only one lonely, dim temple remains in an empty plain, a tiny walker approaching
Shiva walks away alone toward the dusk
Pan across to reveal Daksha in the foreground shadow, glaring after Shiva
Daksha's hard glare, red eyes, name tag
Eyes filling, anger burning: tears and a spreading red glow
Daksha accuses, a trident emblem flaring behind: 'first he cut my father's head'
Fists clenched; the temple behind him dims on 'took away his worship'
A wave of hatred rolls out from him
The dark crimson tide swallows the frame: red eyes in the vignette
Calm: Brahma on a quiet cloud, looking toward us
Eyes to the audience: 'if you were in his place'
Choice one: the bright, honest bow
Choice two: the shadowed smile and the flower
Inviting the comment: 'your answer?' above a half-smiling Brahma
Teaser: a dark, anonymous asura silhouette against warm light (stand-in asura)
He turns toward the devas: an enemy at first glance
Brows soften, a warm glow rising low in the frame at 'heart'
He never refuses: petitioners reach out and he opens his hands
Generosity becomes his undoing; the frame darkens to the end
